Let $\mathbb M=\mathbb R^4$ with coordinates $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and time orientation given by increasing $x^0$. A field configuration is any smooth real function $\phi\in C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R)$; it is off shell, meaning that it is not required to satisfy a field equation. For an integer $s\ge0$, its finite jet at $x$ is the finite tuple $j^s\phi(x)=(\partial^\alpha\phi(x))_{|\alpha|\le s}$, with multi-index derivatives in these coordinates.

An off-shell local polynomial scalar functional is a finite sum
$$F(\phi)=c+\sum_{a=1}^{N}\int_{\mathbb M} f_a(x)\,P_a(j^{s_a}\phi(x))\,d^4x,$$
where $c\in\mathbb C$, $f_a\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb C)$, each $P_a$ is a polynomial in the finitely many jet coordinates, and each $s_a$ is finite. Its support is contained in the compact set $\bigcup_{a=1}^{N}\operatorname{supp}f_a$. The collection of these functionals is denoted $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)$. The involution is $F^*(\phi)=\overline{F(\phi)}$. No physical units or field equation are imposed.

Precisely, $\operatorname{supp}F$ is the set of $x\in\mathbb M$ such that every neighborhood $U$ of $x$ contains the support of some $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R)$ for which $F(\phi+h)\ne F(\phi)$ for some smooth configuration $\phi$. It is closed and is contained in the displayed compact union, so it is compact. This definition is independent of the chosen finite presentation of $F$.

For $r\ge1$, define the $r$th functional derivative by
$$F^{(r)}(\phi)(h_1,\ldots,h_r)=\left.\frac{\partial^r}{\partial t_1\cdots\partial t_r}F\!\left(\phi+\sum_{j=1}^{r}t_jh_j\right)\right|_{t_1=\cdots=t_r=0},\qquad h_j\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R).$$
The finite polynomial expansion makes this a symmetric multilinear form. Repeated integration by parts in each $h_j$ writes it as a compactly supported distribution kernel on the thin diagonal $\{(x,\ldots,x):x\in\mathbb M\}\subset\mathbb M^r$. Integrals use the fixed Minkowski density $d^4x$; all kernels are paired bilinearly with compactly supported smooth tests.

For every $F\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)$, every $\phi\in C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R)$ and every $r\ge1$, the kernel $F^{(r)}(\phi)$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{WF}(F^{(r)}(\phi))\subseteq N^*\Delta_r\setminus0,$$
where $\Delta_r=\{(x,\ldots,x):x\in\mathbb M\}$ and
$$N^*\Delta_r=\{(x,\ldots,x;\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_r):\xi_1+\cdots+\xi_r=0\}.$$
Consequently $F^{(r)}(\phi)$ avoids the all-future and all-past causal cotangent cones and $F$ belongs to $\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)$.

Assume Countable Choice. For field degree $r\ge1$, let $p_1,\ldots,p_r\in\mathbb R^4$ be formal commuting derivative variables, put $P=\sum_a p_a$ and $q_a=p_a-P/r$, and let $\mathcal B_r$ be the vector space of permutation-invariant polynomials in the $q_a$, subject to $\sum_aq_a=0$. A balanced degree-$r$ jet polynomial is
$$B_b(\phi)(x)=\left.b(\partial_{x_1},\ldots,\partial_{x_r})\prod_{a=1}^r\phi(x_a)\right|_{x_1=\cdots=x_r=x},\qquad b\in\mathcal B_r.$$
Thus only relative derivative combinations occur in $b$. Choose a real homogeneous basis of each finite-degree part of $\mathcal B_r$. Every off-shell compactly supported local polynomial functional has a unique expression
$$F(\phi)=c+\sum_{r\ge1}\sum_b\int f_{r,b}(x)B_b(\phi)(x)\,d^4x,$$
with $c\in\mathbb C$, $f_{r,b}\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$, and only finitely many nonzero coefficients. The union of the supports of these coefficient functions equals the functional support, apart from the constant $c$, whose support is empty. The balanced decomposition is compatible with translations, Lorentz transformations and complex conjugation.

Distribution-valued multilinear coefficients prescribed linearly on balanced labels extend consistently to all polynomial jet labels by imposing, in each vertex entry,
$$K(\ldots,\partial_\mu A,\ldots)=\partial_{x_i^\mu}K(\ldots,A,\ldots).$$
After smearing, integration by parts therefore makes the resulting maps independent of the chosen local density presentation. Differentiation adds only a finite derivative order to any finite scaling upper bound.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $D,r\ge1$ be integers, let $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ be distributions on a neighborhood of $0\in\mathbb R^D$, already defined at $0$, and let $a_j\ge0$ be finite real numbers such that $\operatorname{sd}_0(u_j)\le a_j$. Here scaling tests may include the origin. Put $C_j=\{\xi\ne0:(0,\xi)\in\operatorname{WF}(u_j)\}$. Suppose
$$\xi_j\in C_j\cup\{0\},\quad\sum_{j=1}^r\xi_j=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\xi_1=\cdots=\xi_r=0.$$
Then $\prod_{j=1}^r u_j$ is defined on a sufficiently small neighborhood of $0$ and
$$\operatorname{sd}_0\!\left(\prod_{j=1}^r u_j\right)\le\sum_{j=1}^r a_j.$$
The condition is imposed at the scaling center, including the wavefront covectors of the already extended factors there; transversality only on a punctured set is insufficient for this conclusion.

Let $\mathbb M=\mathbb R^4$ have metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and future direction given by increasing $x^0$. Use units $c=1$, so a mass parameter has inverse-length units. Define $x\in J^+(y)$ by $x^0-y^0\ge|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|$ and $x\in J^-(y)$ by $y^0-x^0\ge|\mathbf y-\mathbf x|$; for $A\subseteq\mathbb M$, put $J^\pm(A)=\bigcup_{y\in A}J^\pm(y)$. A field configuration is any smooth real function $\phi$; it is off shell because no field equation is imposed. The allowed local interactions are compactly supported finite polynomial functionals of $\phi$ and finitely many coordinate derivatives, integrated against $d^4x$. The support of a functional $F$ is the closed set of points each of whose neighborhoods contains the support of a compactly supported variation that changes $F$ for some configuration.

For $\Lambda\in SO^+(1,3)$, require $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$, $\det\Lambda=1$, and preservation of the chosen future cone; $SO^+(1,3)$ denotes this identity component. The proper orthochronous Poincare group consists of $\gamma=(a,\Lambda)$ with $a\in\mathbb M$ and $\Lambda\in SO^+(1,3)$. It acts by $(\gamma\cdot\phi)(x)=\phi(\Lambda^{-1}(x-a))$ and $(\gamma\cdot F)(\phi)=F(\gamma^{-1}\cdot\phi)$.

For a distribution on a coordinate chart, its wavefront set consists of the nonzero cotangent directions where every compact localization fails to have a rapidly decreasing Fourier transform in every conic neighborhood. Covectors are future or past causal when their metric-dual vectors are causal with the indicated time orientation; a nonzero causal covector has a nonzero time component. Write $\Delta=\{(x,x):x\in\mathbb M\}$ and $N^*\Delta=\{(x,\xi;x,-\xi):\xi\ne0\}$. Write $(x,\xi)\sim(y,\zeta)$ when both covectors are nonzero null and cotangent to the same null straight line, with parallel transport carrying $\xi$ to $\zeta$. Precisely, for $x\ne y$ there must be a future-directed nonconstant affinely parametrized null straight line $\gamma$ and parameters $s,t$ in either order with $x=\gamma(s)$, $y=\gamma(t)$ and a real $\lambda\ne0$ such that $\xi=\lambda\eta(\dot\gamma(s),\cdot)$ and $\zeta=\lambda\eta(\dot\gamma(t),\cdot)$. When $x=y$, require $\xi=\zeta$ and allow every nonzero null covector. This relation is unsigned: the future first-covector condition below selects $\lambda>0$, while the Feynman past branch selects $\lambda<0$. A fixed free scalar input consists of $m\ge0$, a two-point distribution $W$ satisfying
$$P_xW=P_yW=0,\qquad P=-\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b+m^2,$$
and the positive-frequency null wavefront condition
$$\operatorname{WF}(W)=\mathcal C^+:=\{(x,\xi;y,-\eta):(x,\xi)\sim(y,\eta),\ \xi\text{ future null}\}.$$
For a two-point distribution $U$, set $U^{\mathsf T}(x,y)=U(y,x)$ and let $U^*$ be complex conjugation. Assume $W$ is invariant under translations and $SO^+(1,3)$, satisfies $W-W^{\mathsf T}=iE$ for a fixed distribution $E$ supported where $x-y$ is causal, and satisfies $W^*=W^{\mathsf T}$.

The prescribed scalar time-ordered contraction input is a symmetric distribution $H_F\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb M^2)$ invariant under translations and $SO^+(1,3)$, equal to $W(x,y)$ on the open set $x^0>y^0$ and to $W(y,x)$ on $y^0>x^0$. The two prescriptions agree on spacelike-separated open supports because $E$ is supported on causal pairs. Translation invariance gives $H_F(x,y)=h_F(x-y)$ and $W(x,y)=w(x-y)$. For a distribution $T$ on $\mathbb R^4$, set $T_\rho(\varphi)=\rho^{-4}T(\varphi(\cdot/\rho))$ and define $\operatorname{sd}_0(T)$ as the infimum of real $\omega$ for which $\rho^\omega T_\rho\to0$ on each fixed test as $\rho\downarrow0$. Require $\operatorname{sd}_0(h_F),\operatorname{sd}_0(w)\le2$ and
$$\operatorname{WF}(H_F)\subseteq\Gamma_F:=N^*\Delta\cup\{(x,\xi;y,-\eta):x\ne y,\ (x,\xi)\sim(y,\eta),\ \xi\text{ future null if }x\in J^+(y),\ \xi\text{ past null if }x\in J^-(y)\}.$$
This is fixed conditional data: it does not claim existence of $W$ or $H_F$, and it does not define any singular restriction or product of $H_F$ on a diagonal.

For $r\ge1$, $F^{(r)}(\phi)$ denotes the distribution kernel on $\mathbb M^r$ of the mixed variation in $r$ compactly supported smooth directions, and set $F^{(0)}(\phi)=F(\phi)$. Define $\deg F$ as the largest positive $r$ with $F^{(r)}\ne0$, or $0$ if all positive-order derivative kernels vanish; in particular $\deg0=0$. The class $\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)$ consists of finite polynomial functionals with compactly supported derivative kernels such that every nonzero wavefront tuple of each derivative kernel avoids both the cone of tuples whose entries are all future causal and the cone of tuples whose entries are all past causal; zero entries in either cone are allowed. For $F,G$ in this class, define
$$F\star_WG=\sum_{r=0}^{\min(\deg F,\deg G)}\frac{\hbar^r}{r!}\left\langle F^{(r)}(\phi)\otimes G^{(r)}(\phi),W^{\otimes r}\right\rangle,$$
using distribution products and pushforwards under the stated wavefront transversality conditions, with the $r=0$ pairing interpreted as the pointwise product $F(\phi)G(\phi)$. Here $\hbar$ is a formal indeterminate, and Countable Choice is assumed for the supplier theorem defining these contractions.

A scalar time-ordered system is a sequence of symmetric multilinear maps
$$T_n:\big(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)\big)^n\longrightarrow \mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket,\qquad T_0=1,\quad T_1=\operatorname{id}.$$
For $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ put $S_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}\operatorname{supp}F_i$ and $F_I=(F_i)_{i\in I}$. Causal factorization requires
$$T_n(F_1,\ldots,F_n)=T_{|I|}(F_I)\star_W T_{|I^c|}(F_{I^c})$$
for every nonempty proper $I$ such that $S_I\cap J^-(S_{I^c})=\varnothing$; an empty block is the unit.

Field independence means that each numerical graph distribution is independent of the background field $\phi$; all $\phi$-dependence enters through the vertex kernels $F_i^{(r)}(\phi)$. In the graph expansion of $T_n$, vertices are labeled by $1,\ldots,n$ and an edge between distinct vertices contracts one derivative slot at each endpoint by $H_F$. A graph is a finite loopless multigraph, so parallel edges are allowed; if $r_{ij}$ edges join vertices $i$ and $j$, the Wick coefficient for that choice includes $\hbar^{\sum_{i<j}r_{ij}}/\prod_{i<j}r_{ij}!$. Finite-order local jet derivatives may act on incident edge kernels. Each coefficient is a finite sum of such contractions, since every input has finite polynomial degree. No graph term uses a singular product at a diagonal before extension.

For $n\ge2$, use relative coordinates $z_i=x_i-x_n$ ($1\le i<n$), so the total diagonal corresponds to $0\in\mathbb R^{4(n-1)}$. The relative scaling degree $\delta_\Gamma$ of a numerical graph distribution is defined by the same positive-dilation rule above in this relative dimension. The scaling condition is imposed compatibly with integration by parts in the local functionals. First write every local density in its unique balanced-jet representative, in which the derivative variables at a degree-$r$ vertex are the relative combinations $q_a=p_a-r^{-1}\sum_bp_b$. At the extension stage, numerical coefficients on independent balanced labels admit extensions across the total diagonal preserving their actual scaling degree; the final normalization conditions below are imposed within the engineering upper bounds. General jet labels are recovered by total coordinate differentiation of the already extended full coefficients and by linearity; this includes differentiation of the remaining field jets. For a primitive differentiated graph the required upper scaling bound is the engineering degree
$$B_\Gamma=2|E(\Gamma)|+\sum_e|\alpha_e|.$$
For a graph containing proper subgraphs, use a finite upper bound obtained by causal block induction from the edge degrees and the finite derivative orders of the chosen lower-order local counterterms; total derivatives add their orders to that bound. Any two extensions of a fixed punctured coefficient with upper bound $B_\Gamma$ differ by derivatives $\partial^\beta\delta_0$ of order $|\beta|\le\lfloor B_\Gamma-4(n-1)\rfloor$ when $B_\Gamma\ge4(n-1)$, and agree when $B_\Gamma<4(n-1)$. The allowed counterterms must also satisfy the stated linearity and derivative identities. For the analytic degree-preserving extension family of an independent balanced coefficient, its actual degree replaces $B_\Gamma$ in this ambiguity bound. A differentiated coefficient is not required to retain the exact scaling degree of a punctured linear combination that vanishes: total differentiation may force a contact term at the diagonal.

Covariance requires $T_n(\gamma\cdot F_1,\ldots,\gamma\cdot F_n)=\gamma\cdot T_n(F_1,\ldots,F_n)$ for each proper orthochronous Poincare transformation. Fix the Lorentz Lie-algebra convention $[J_i,J_j]=\epsilon_{ijk}J_k$, $[J_i,K_j]=\epsilon_{ijk}K_j$, and $[K_i,K_j]=-\epsilon_{ijk}J_i$. For a formal coupling $g$, define coefficientwise
$$\mathcal S_g(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(ig/\hbar)^n}{n!}T_n(V,\ldots,V).$$
The anti-time-ordered series is $\overline{\mathcal S}_g(V):=\mathcal S_g(V)^*$, where the involution conjugates scalar coefficients, fixes real $g,\hbar$, and reverses the order of factors; $W^*=W^{\mathsf T}$ gives $(F\star_WG)^*=G^*\star_WF^*$. Formal unitarity requires $\overline{\mathcal S}_g(V)\star_W\mathcal S_g(V)=1$ for every real $V=V^*$. At each $g$-order, coefficients are finite Laurent polynomials in $\hbar$ before cancellation and are compared algebraically; there is no analytic convergence, positivity of formal coefficients, adiabatic limit, or gauge/Ward identity in this contract.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice and fix admissible scalar free data as defined by the local time-ordered product contract. Fix a finite loopless multigraph $\Gamma$ with $n\ge2$ labeled vertices, parallel edges allowed, and a finite multi-index derivative $\alpha_e$ on each edge $e$. Suppose every proper partial-diagonal subgraph has already received a translation-invariant extension obeying the scaling upper bounds of that contract by induction on its number of vertices. Then the numerical graph distribution on the complement of the total diagonal has a finite upper scaling bound in the $4(n-1)$ relative coordinates. For a primitive graph, with no proper divergent subgraph, the bound is
$$\operatorname{sd}_0(t_\Gamma)\le 2|E(\Gamma)|+\sum_{e\in E(\Gamma)}|\alpha_e|.$$
For a graph with proper subgraphs, the same induction gives a finite bound obtained from this edge estimate and the finitely many derivative orders of its lower-order local counterterms.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix any admissible flat scalar free datum and local scalar polynomial class as defined by the local time-ordered product contract. Then there exists a sequence of symmetric multilinear maps $T_n$ satisfying that contract at every finite perturbative order. At order $n$, each numerical graph distribution has a finite upper scaling bound in the $4(n-1)$ relative coordinates. At the analytic extension stage, independent balanced coefficients admit extensions preserving their actual scaling degree; total-derivative labels and the final local normalizations obey the engineering scaling upper bounds prescribed by the contract. For a fixed punctured coefficient with bound $B_\Gamma$, the extension ambiguity is contained in the finite span of derivatives of the diagonal delta distribution of order at most $\lfloor B_\Gamma-4(n-1)\rfloor$ when $B_\Gamma\ge4(n-1)$, and is zero when $B_\Gamma<4(n-1)$, subject also to the linearity and derivative identities. For the analytic degree-preserving extension family of an independent balanced coefficient, one can use its actual degree in place of $B_\Gamma$. Thus the coefficients form a formal series only; no convergence in the coupling, adiabatic limit, positivity claim, or gauge/Ward identity is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. For two scalar time-ordered systems $T$ and $T'$ satisfying the local scalar contract for the same free data and with $T_0=T'_0=1$, $T_1=T'_1=\operatorname{id}$, define their normalized formal S-maps by
$$\mathcal S(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n!}T_n(V,\ldots,V),\qquad \mathcal S'(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n!}T'_n(V,\ldots,V).$$
There is a unique formal map $Z(V)=V+O(V^2)$ from local polynomial functionals to local polynomial functionals such that $Z(0)=0$, $dZ_0=\operatorname{id}$, $Z$ preserves supports and scalar Poincare covariance, and
$$\mathcal S'(V)=\mathcal S(Z(V))$$
coefficientwise. Such maps compose, and each has a recursively defined formal inverse; hence they form a group under composition.

For all admissible flat scalar free data, time-ordered maps on the full off-shell finite-jet local functional class can preserve the exact scaling degree of every punctured differentiated numerical coefficient and its linear combinations, while being independent of the chosen density presentation. In particular, a differentiated coefficient that vanishes off the diagonal would have to extend as zero.

Assume AC and Countable Choice, fix admissible flat scalar free data and a local scalar polynomial class under a scalar formal time-ordering theorem, and work conditionally in a time-ordering scheme satisfying that theorem's statement. At order $n$, let $\mathcal K_n$ be an $s,d_H$-stable subcomplex of the compactly supported local-form spaces defined earlier, with $\mathcal K_n^{0,4}$ exactly the allowed local counterterm densities. For each ghost number $r$, put
$$\mathscr F_n^r:=\mathcal K_n^{r,4}/d_H\mathcal K_n^{r,3},$$
the local-functional quotient formed using this same subcomplex, and let $\mathscr F_n^\bullet\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$ denote formal power series. Let $\mathcal W_\hbar=s+\sum_{j\ge1}\hbar^j\mathcal W_j$ be an odd formal operator of ghost number one on this module, with $\mathcal W_\hbar^2=0$ and leading coefficient the induced $s$. Let $X\in\mathscr F_n^0\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$ and suppose its first possible breaking is
$$\mathcal W_\hbar X=\hbar^n\mathcal A+O(\hbar^{n+1}),\qquad n\ge1,\qquad \mathcal A=[a_4]_{\mathscr F_n},$$
where $\hbar$ is a formal indeterminate, $O(\hbar^{n+1})$ means terms of formal degree at least $n+1$, every lower coefficient vanishes, and $a_4\in\mathcal K_n^{1,4}$ is a compactly supported local four-form of ghost number one. Then $s a_4$ is $d_H$-exact within $\mathcal K_n$. The counterterm shift $X\mapsto X-\hbar^n[b_4]_{\mathscr F_n}$, with $b_4\in\mathcal K_n^{0,4}$, cancels the order-$n$ breaking in $\mathscr F_n^1$ if and only if
$$[a_4]_{s|d_H}=0\quad\text{in}\quad H^{1,4}(s|d_H;\mathcal K_n).$$
This is a conditional obstruction statement. Locality of $a_4$, nilpotence of the formal Ward differential, and admissibility of the counterterm space are assumptions; the result does not establish a quantum action principle.

Assume Countable Choice.

Let $\mathbb M=\mathbb R^4$ have Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. A scalar local polynomial functional is a finite sum
$$F(\phi)=c+\sum_{j=1}^{N}\int_{\mathbb M} f_j(x)P_j(j^{s_j}\phi(x))\,d^4x,$$
where $N$ is a finite nonnegative integer, $\phi\in C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R)$, $c\in\mathbb C$, and $f_j\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb C)$. For a finite integer $s_j\ge0$, the $s_j$-jet is $j^{s_j}\phi(x)=(\partial^\alpha\phi(x))_{\alpha\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}^4,\,|\alpha|\le s_j}$; each $P_j$ is a complex polynomial in these finitely many jet coordinates. This is the local functional class used by the supplied scalar time-ordered system.

For every mass label $m\ge0$, suppose a normalized scalar time-ordered system $T_n^{(m)}$ with the same local scalar contract is supplied. Define its coefficientwise formal S-map by
$$\mathcal S_m(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n!}T_n^{(m)}(V,\ldots,V),\qquad T_0^{(m)}=1,\quad T_1^{(m)}=\operatorname{id}.$$
The series is formal in the interaction degree; no analytic convergence is asserted.

Use units $c=\hbar=1$, so the mass label $m$ has mass dimension one. The scale parameter $\rho>0$ is dimensionless. On scalar field configurations put
$$(C_\rho\phi)(x)=\rho^{-1}\phi(\rho^{-1}x),$$
the engineering scaling of a four-dimensional scalar field. On a family of mass-labelled functionals or maps $A=(A_m)_{m\ge0}$, define
$$(\sigma_\rho A)_m=C_\rho^*(A_{\rho^{-1}m}),\qquad (C_\rho^*F)(\phi)=F(C_{\rho^{-1}}\phi).$$
Extend this action coefficientwise to formal series and maps. It obeys $\sigma_1=\operatorname{id}$ and $\sigma_{\rho\tau}=\sigma_\rho\sigma_\tau$; the mass label scales as $m\mapsto\rho m$. The dilation sends compact supports to compact supports and normalizes the proper orthochronous Poincare action.

Assume for each $\rho>0$ that $\mathcal S$ and its scale conjugate $\sigma_\rho\mathcal S\sigma_\rho^{-1}$ are both normalized scalar time-ordered systems for the same mass-indexed free data after the stated mass relabelling. Define $Z_\rho$ to be the unique formal local map with identity linear term satisfying
$$\sigma_\rho\mathcal S\sigma_\rho^{-1}=\mathcal S\circ Z_\rho.$$
Here $Z_\rho(V)=V+O(V^2)$ means that all terms after the linear term have interaction degree at least two. This is a conditional definition: no existence of a time-ordered system for any particular model is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice.

Let $Z_\rho$ be the mass-indexed formal renormalization map defined for the scale action $\sigma_\rho$, $\rho>0$. For all $\rho,\tau>0$,
$$Z_{\rho\tau}=Z_\rho\circ\bigl(\sigma_\rho Z_\tau\sigma_\rho^{-1}\bigr).$$
If conjugation by every $\sigma_\rho$ acts trivially on the renormalization subgroup, this reduces to $Z_{\rho\tau}=Z_\rho\circ Z_\tau$. In the general mass-dependent case the twisted formula is the claim; no one-parameter subgroup law is asserted.

Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of isomorphism classes of finite nonempty rooted trees. A rooted tree is a finite connected acyclic graph with one distinguished vertex, the root; each edge is oriented from the vertex nearer the root (the parent) to the vertex farther from the root (the child). A forest is a finite multiset of rooted trees, including the empty forest $1$. Let $H=\mathbb Q[\mathcal T]$ be the commutative polynomial algebra generated by $\mathcal T$; its monomial basis consists of forests, and the degree of a forest is its total number of vertices.

For a rooted tree $t$, an admissible cut is a subset $C$ of its edges meeting every root-to-leaf path in at most one edge. Removing the edges of $C$ leaves one component containing the root; denote it by $R_C(t)$. The components on the child side of the cut edges form a forest denoted by $P_C(t)$. For the empty edge cut, set $P_{\varnothing}(t)=1$ and $R_{\varnothing}(t)=t$. Define the coproduct on a tree generator by
$$\Delta(t)=t\otimes1+\sum_{C\text{ admissible}}P_C(t)\otimes R_C(t),$$
where the sum includes the empty edge cut and retains multiplicities of distinct edge subsets. The term $t\otimes1$ is the separate virtual full cut above the root. Extend $\Delta$ multiplicatively to forests. Define $\varepsilon(1)=1$ and $\varepsilon(F)=0$ for every nonempty forest $F$. This specifies the rooted-tree subtraction model; it does not assert a canonical rooted-tree Hopf algebra or a graph-to-forest map for every Feynman graph.

Let $K$ be a commutative unital $\mathbb Q$-algebra and let $\epsilon$ be a formal indeterminate. The Laurent-series algebra $A=K((\epsilon))$ consists of series $\sum_{n\ge N}a_n\epsilon^n$ for some integer $N$, with coefficients in $K$. Put $A_-=\epsilon^{-1}K[\epsilon^{-1}]$ (finite sums of strictly negative powers) and $A_+=\{\sum_{n\ge0}a_n\epsilon^n:a_n\in K\}$ (formal series of nonnegative powers). Then $A=A_-\oplus A_+$ as a $K$-module, and both summands are subalgebras, with $1\in A_+$. Define $R:A\to A_-$ by retaining exactly the strictly negative powers; $1-R$ is the projection onto $A_+$. The parameter $\epsilon$ is formal and carries no physical or empirical interpretation in this definition.

Let $K$ be a commutative unital $\mathbb Q$-algebra, let $\epsilon$ be formal, and put $A=K((\epsilon))$ with projection $R$ onto strictly negative powers. For all $x,y\in A$, $R$ satisfies
$$R(x)R(y)=R\bigl(R(x)y+xR(y)-xy\bigr).$$

Let $\mathcal T$ be the isomorphism classes of finite nonempty rooted trees and $H=\mathbb Q[\mathcal T]$ their commutative polynomial algebra, graded by total vertices. An admissible cut is an edge subset meeting each root-to-leaf path at most once; $P_C(t)$ is its child-side forest and $R_C(t)$ its root-side tree. Use the coproduct $\Delta(t)=t\otimes1+\sum_C P_C(t)\otimes R_C(t)$, with the sum over admissible cuts including the empty cut, and counit $\varepsilon(1)=1$, $\varepsilon(F)=0$ for nonempty forests. The algebra $H$ is a connected graded bialgebra. Let $u$ be the algebra unit map and $m$ forest multiplication; use convolution $f*g=m(f\otimes g)\Delta$ on endomorphisms of $H$, with unit $u\varepsilon$. It has a unique two-sided convolution inverse $S$ of its identity map. For every rooted tree $t$ of positive degree,
$$S(1)=1,\qquad S(t)=-t-\sum_{\substack{C\ne\varnothing\\ C\text{ admissible}}}S(P_C(t))R_C(t).$$
The recursion is finite because each factor in every nonempty-cut term has fewer vertices than $t$. The antipode is multiplicative on forests. This is a theorem about the specified rooted-tree model and does not identify arbitrary Feynman graphs with rooted trees.

Let $\mathcal T$ be the isomorphism classes of finite nonempty rooted trees and $H=\mathbb Q[\mathcal T]$ their connected graded commutative Hopf algebra, graded by total vertices. Its coproduct is $\Delta(t)=t\otimes1+\sum_C P_C(t)\otimes R_C(t)$, where $C$ ranges over edge subsets meeting each root-to-leaf path at most once (including the empty cut), $P_C(t)$ is the child-side forest, and $R_C(t)$ is the root-side component; let $S$ be its antipode. Put $H_+=\bigoplus_{n>0}H_n$. Let $K$ be a commutative unital $\mathbb Q$-algebra, let $\epsilon$ be formal, and let $A=K((\epsilon))=A_-\oplus A_+$ split into strictly negative and nonnegative powers, with $R$ the projection onto $A_-$. A character is a unital algebra homomorphism $\phi:H\to A$. For each positive-degree homogeneous $h$, write $\widetilde\Delta(h)=\Delta(h)-h\otimes1-1\otimes h$ and define recursively
$$B_\phi(h)=\phi(h)+\sum_{\widetilde\Delta(h)}\phi_-(h_{(1)})\phi(h_{(2)}),\qquad \phi_-(1)=1,\qquad \phi_-(h)=-R B_\phi(h).$$
The sum is over the finite reduced coproduct and the recursion is degreewise finite. Define convolution by $f*g=m_A(f\otimes g)\Delta$, where $m_A$ and $u_A$ are the multiplication and unit maps of $A$, and put $\phi_+=\phi_-*\phi$. Then $\phi_-$ and $\phi_+$ are characters, $\phi_-(H_+)\subseteq A_-$ and $\phi_+(H)\subseteq A_+$, and the convolution inverse $\phi_-^{-1}=\phi_-\circ S$ exists with
$$\phi=\phi_-^{-1}*\phi_+.$$
This is an algebraic factorization for characters; it does not assert a graph-to-rooted-tree identification for actual Feynman graphs.

Let $t=\log\rho\in\mathbb R$ be the dimensionless logarithmic scale parameter associated with $\rho>0$. Take $g(t)$ to be a dimensionless real coupling, and prescribe dimensionless constants $b,g_0\in\mathbb R$ in the truncated scalar initial-value problem
$$\frac{dg}{dt}=bg^2,\qquad g(0)=g_0.$$
If $c:=bg_0=0$, its unique maximal real solution is $g(t)=g_0$ on $\mathbb R$. If $c\ne0$, its unique maximal solution through $t=0$ is
$$g(t)=\frac{g_0}{1-bg_0t}$$
on $(-\infty,c^{-1})$ when $c>0$ and on $(c^{-1},\infty)$ when $c<0$.

For the formal beta series $\beta(g)=bg^2+O(g^3)$, let $\widetilde g=\Phi(g)=g+ag^2+O(g^3)$ be an invertible formal change of dimensionless coupling, with dimensionless $a\in\mathbb R$. Here $O(g^k)$ denotes a formal power series whose terms have degree at least $k$, and $\Phi'$ is the termwise formal derivative. The transformed vector field is
$$\widetilde\beta(\widetilde g)=\bigl(\Phi'(g)\beta(g)\bigr)\big|_{g=\Phi^{-1}(\widetilde g)}.$$
Its quadratic coefficient is $b$. The real ODE is exact only for the displayed truncation; neither it nor the formal scheme-change statement determines $b$ from a QFT graph or bounds omitted higher-order terms. Its pole is a property of this truncated equation, not a theorem about an ultraviolet completion.
